title: Entitlement Reconciliation and Drift Mitigation Plan for RBAC v2
summary: Practical plan to reconcile current permission state to RBAC v2, how to detect and remediate entitlement drift, proposed audit log schema extensions for evidence automation, and a phased SIEM export strategy that preserves forensic fidelity while controlling volume.
body:
Purpose
This doc captures an operationally focused reconciliation and rollout plan for RBAC v2. Goals: 1) safe, observable migration from current entitlement surface to the new model, 2) automated evidence capture for compliance, and 3) drift detection/mitigation after rollout so we don’t regress to an inconsistent permission state.

Context and motivation
- Current observations: permissions are unevenly applied across services, there are stale role bindings on older projects, and ad-hoc service accounts with broad scopes.
- Constraints: customers and internal teams expect no service disruption; audit trail continuity is required for compliance; SIEM ingestion costs and index volumes must remain bounded.

High-level approach
1) Capability grounding: define canonical capabilities (fine-grained actions) and map all existing roles/policies to those capabilities. This produces a capability matrix per product area.
2) Shadow reconciliation: run a read-only reconciliation agent (perm-shadow) that computes desired vs observed entitlements nightly and writes diffs to the evidence stream. No changes are made automatically in shadow mode.
3) Targeted remediation runs (opt-in): remediation jobs are run by owners after review; each remediation is a small, auditable change with a rollback path.
4) Continuous reconciler and drift detector: after move to RBAC v2, a sampler watches for entropy in bindings and surfaces anomalies to SRE/Platform for action.

Roles and responsibilities
- Security: stewardship of capability taxonomy and audit schema.
- Platform/Infra: run reconciliation agents, apply platform-level role changes.
- Product teams: own the mapping of product roles to canonical capabilities; accept or reject remediations.
- Compliance: validate evidence exports and retention.

RBAC v2-specific constructs we will use
- Capability ID (cap_id): stable string identifier for a single atomic operation (e.g., storage.object.read).
- Binding fingerprint: short hash of (principal, resource, capabilities) used for fast diffing and sampling.
- Epoch tags: change batches labeled with an epoch id to group reconciliation work for auditing.

Audit/event schema (proposed minimal fields for evidence automation)
Each reconciliation or entitlement change event emitted to evidence pipeline will be a single line JSON in the event stream (we will map to SIEM fields on export). Fields below are plain keys for the event JSON.
- event_id: uuid
- timestamp: iso8601
- event_type: {"reconciliation-diff"|"binding-change"|"remediation-run"|"drift-alert"}
- actor: principal id that requested the change (user/service)
- actor_type: {"human","service","system"}
- resource: resource canonical id (service:resource:path)
- capabilities: comma-separated capability IDs applied or removed
- before_fingerprint: binding-fingerprint (or empty)
- after_fingerprint: binding-fingerprint (or empty)
- epoch: reconciliation epoch id
- evidence_refs: comma-separated artefact ids (proof snapshots, screenshots, PR/issue links)
- change_reason: free text (owner provided)
- change_ticket: optional ticket id (Jira/Linear)
- retention_tier: {"primary","archive"}
- sampling_hint: {"full","sampled:1/1000","none"}  # consumer guidance for SIEM export

Notes on schema choices
- Keep all fields shallow and string typed to make mapping to older pipelines easy.
- Use fingerprinting to dedupe identical bindings across many resources to control SIEM volume.
- Include evidence_refs so that linkability back into PRs/issues is preserved for audits.

SIEM export strategy
We need to balance fidelity and cost. Plan: tiered export.
- Tier 1 (full fidelity): high-risk scope (org-level admin bindings, customer-facing production projects) -> export full events.
- Tier 2 (sampled): mid-risk resources -> use sampling_hint to export 1/1000 events unless a drift-alert raises the priority.
- Tier 3 (aggregate): low-risk infra/test namespaces -> export aggregates (counts, unique fingerprint lists) daily.
Mapping examples for Splunk/Elastic fields (flat key names):
- event.action -> event_type
- user.id -> actor
- user.type -> actor_type
- object.id -> resource
- object.capabilities -> capabilities
- change.id -> event_id
- metadata.epoch -> epoch
- metadata.fingerprint_before -> before_fingerprint
- metadata.fingerprint_after -> after_fingerprint
- evidence.links -> evidence_refs
- notes.short -> change_reason

Reconciliation algorithm (practical description)
1) Inventory: gather bindings from IAM, service-specific ACLs, and historical PR/commit references. Normalize to canonical resource ids.
2) Map existing roles to capability sets using the capability matrix. Some roles will map to multiple capability sets — produce a superset.
3) Desired state computation: prefer least-privilege proposals derived from recent observed usage (last 90 days) + product owner overrides.
4) Diff generation: compute added/removed capabilities per principal per resource; store diffs in evidence stream with epoch tag.
5) Owner review queue: product owners see diffs in the Console; they can accept, modify, or reject per-item.
6) Remediation: small, single-role-change commits that include rollback steps and are recorded as binding-change events.

Drift detection and mitigation
- Drift signals: (a) unexpected new binding fingerprints, (b) increased cardinality of principals for a capability, (c) bindings reappearing after removal, (d) use-pattern mismatch (binding exists but no usage).
- Automated reactions: low-risk anomalies -> auto-ticket creation and sampling; high-risk anomalies -> ephemeral lockdown (temporary deny) and pager to on-call.
- Lockdown safety: lockdowns are scoped to a single resource and emit a 'change_ticket' with remediation run id; platform SRE must approve auto-lockdown within 30 minutes or system rolls back.

Evidence automation workflow
- Reconciliation agent produces signed snapshots (tarball + manifest hash) stored in evidence-bucket with path: {org}/{epoch}/{resource}/{event_id}.
- Evidence snapshot metadata is emitted as evidence_refs in the event JSON. SIEM export points to this reference (not the snapshot itself).
- For audit requests, compliance can retrieve the full snapshot via signed URL and verify manifest hash.

Retention and sampling policy
- Primary retention (90 days): full event records for Tier 1 and Tier 2 drift-alerts.
- Archive (7 years): manifests and fingerprints plus links to evidence snapshots (snapshots themselves may be persisted to cold storage).
- Sampling: default 1/1000 for mid/low tiers, override rules for customer-critical resources.

Rollout plan (phased)
Phase 0: Preparation (2–4 weeks)
- Finalize capability taxonomy for two pilot product areas (Storage and Console).
- Build mapping tool and seed matrix.
- Stand up perm-shadow in read-only mode for the pilots.

Phase 1: Pilot shadow (4–8 weeks)
- Run nightly shadow, surface diffs to owners, gather feedback.
- Ship Console views to let owners filter, annotate diffs, and attach tickets.
- Tune sampling and Tier definitions.

Phase 2: Controlled remediation (6–10 weeks)
- Accept small remediations in pilot area with opt-in automation (owner-triggered).
- Start exporting Tier 1 events to SIEM; validate mapping and retention.

Phase 3: Gradual expansion (rolling, 3–6 months)
- Expand to additional product areas in parallel waves, each with its own pilot owner group.
- Introduce drift detector rules and auto-ticketing.

Phase 4: Enforcement and continuous mode (ongoing)
- Move reconciler into continuous enforcement for low-risk bindings (automatic short-lived denies for high-risk anomalies).
- Maintain audit export and cold-archive pipeline for evidence.

Risk analysis and mitigations
- Risk: false positives causing service disruption. Mitigation: start in shadow, require owner approval for changes, and keep short rollback windows.
- Risk: SIEM cost overrun due to high event volume. Mitigation: fingerprint dedupe, tiered export, and sampling.
- Risk: owners ignore reconciliation queue. Mitigation: run periodic executive summaries and require acknowledgment for high-risk diffs.

Open questions (to resolve before Phase 1 start)
- Master list: what exact cardinality thresholds define Tier 1 vs Tier 2?
- Cost model: how do we bill SIEM overages and which budget owner pays?
- How to map service-level ACLs that don’t cleanly translate to cap_id model (examples: legacy batch jobs)?

Next actions (owner: Priya)
- Finalize capability taxonomy draft with Ethan and Maya by 2025-11-24.
- Provision perm-shadow cluster and run 1-week smoke test by 2025-12-08.
- Draft Console review UI wireframes and share with product-hosted-api by 2025-12-15.
- Confirm retention and cold-archive storage budget with finance/legal by 2026-01-10.

Appendix A — Example event (single-line JSON representation)
{"event_id":"evt-0a1b2c","timestamp":"2026-02-01T18:22:43Z","event_type":"reconciliation-diff","actor":"system:perm-shadow","actor_type":"system","resource":"storage:bucket:prod-reports","capabilities":"storage.object.read,storage.object.delete","before_fingerprint":"f7a9c3","after_fingerprint":"f7a9c3-2","epoch":"epoch-2026-02-01-1","evidence_refs":"s3://evidence/12345/evt-0a1b2c/manifest.json","change_reason":"de-dupe legacy role mapping","change_ticket":"JIRA-4122","retention_tier":"primary","sampling_hint":"sampled:1/1000"}

Appendix B — Short glossary
- Capability grounding: converting coarse roles to atomic capability ids.
- Fingerprint: stable short hash for quick equality checks across many resources.
- Epoch: reconciliation run grouping id.

Notes to reviewers
Please call out if any field in the audit schema prevents mapping to our current SIEM (ElasticCloud) or to downstream analytics. If you are an owner of a product area and want to be in the pilot, comment below or ping priya@redwood.com on Slack.

---
Working draft: expect iteration. This doc mixes design, ops steps, and TODOs to be actionable for the pilot teams.
decisions: Emit shallow, flat event schema to ease consumption by legacy pipelines.
Use fingerprinting to reduce SIEM payload and dedupe identical bindings.
Start with a shadow-first approach and opt-in remediation to reduce risk.
